correctness.rationale: The integral polynomial-ring proof proves divisibility at N_a and failure at N_a−1 for every odd prime power using exact S-adic order t of S^(p^d)/p modulo p. The analogous J^2=2J argument proves the exact two-adic index. Group-ring CRT then gives the maximum across all root factors and all prime powers; the cyclic basic generator attains it. The distinct nilpotency and finite-graph check algorithms agree in 65 and 87 cases, respectively, as secondary evidence.

originality.rationale: The exact odd-prime-power bound equality is explicitly conjectural in Lewis–Tefft 2024, their 2026 final published article, and Tefft 2025 dissertation. The proof supplies a missing sharp lower-bound argument for all p odd, a>=2 and compatible even lengths. Earlier prime-modulus, odd-length and two-power cases and a known modulo-four transient distribution are attributed, not presented as independently new. The inspected record identifies no stronger covering result; bibliographic exhaustiveness is not claimed.
residual_risks: Full text of Breuer (1999) was not accessed; only later primary references and search metadata were compared.
Unindexed equivalences in older cyclic group-ring nilpotency theory remain possible.
A separate 2025 period-related work by Lewis and Tefft was identified by abstract only; it concerns periods, and its full text was not used to assert noncoverage.

value.rationale: This resolves a concrete, explicitly stated conjecture retained in the 2026 final paper, for infinitely many odd-prime-power moduli and every even tuple length divisible by the prime. An exact structural filtration demonstrates why the conjectured upper bound is sharp and completes the full local-to-global maximum-transient formula. This is not an arbitrary finite numerical improvement, renaming, or simple prime-modulus corollary.
